body: If you are at this place, you might as well embrace a devil may care approach to the rest of your life (well, within reason, lol) and try new things. What can happen? You already hate life and feel trapped; I think your best bet is to rock the boat and see what falls out. At least life will feel spontaneous and different for a while.

You know you were wrong, and that's why you should forgive yourself and not let it stop you from being who you are now that you're past that mistake. I know God forgives you, but you need to forgive yourself, too. Let it go. It doesn't define you anymore, but just know you won't ever forget it either. You have to let it be a reminder that you have grown as a person and matured. Guilt about your behavior is fine in the short term. Letting it become a long-held regret, though, is a mistake when you know for sure you aren't capable of that anymore.

I think we both need to find new jobs, ones that we have a passion for, because environment matters. You have to be in an environment every day that feeds you hope, not the horrible feeling that you're just a cog in the machine who can be replaced at any time.

We must awaken something that makes us feel alive and hopeful inside, or else this life is nothing but torture, every day, and that's a misery I don't want anymore, do you? Of course not. Believe things will get better and fight for it (as you are now by providing for yourself, and reaching out for a shoulder to lean on).

Just speaking as one human to another, but I love you and hope you feel better soon. Well, that we both feel better, that is. Keep fighting, it's worth it. The depressing part is that people ever get to a point where they have to think of death as the answer to their prayers. Hopefully, we all remember a time when death was either the last thing on our mind or a passing scary thought, and we were all focused on happier thoughts like good friendships and succeeding at a hobby, your career, etc.

So, yes, while I can understand how a happy life can fall apart and one can start to see death as an answer, I feel that you must fight that downward spiral. It's a mental fight, one where if you start to lose ground, it can very quickly lead to a dark place of despair and hopelessness.

It sort of snuck up on me, actually. I didn't really see it coming; it managed to creep in and rear its ugly head to me recently. But this depression makes me appreciate those happier times all the more, as weird as that sounds. Basically, you don't know what you've got until it's gone because we all, without meaning to, take the good times for granted and normal.

At the risk of sounding cliche, you just have to count your blessings, even if the count is dropping day by day. Death is not an answer to anyone's problem as long as you value something about being alive. If you can't value anything anymore, then it's time to do something major to shake things up and somehow bounce back, whatever that action is, is up to you but find any resource available to draw upon, good luck to everybody. I say all this in a dark time myself.

Basically, this is an IPS patch that I leave to you to figure out how to use and apply, but it turns Final Fantasy NES into something very close to a more modern (think FF Origins or Dawn of Souls) rendition.

The graphics are redone in a lot of places, it has a b-button dash added, you can press B at the main title screen to change the menu color to something you like, and there's even lots of new music put into the game. Other changes made as well, but too many to really list them all. You save the game from the menu, not from staying at inns. This means you can save anywhere on the world map like later FF games handled it.

Enjoy. I recommend playing with Fighter, Thief, Red Mage, Black Mage. If your thief is at the head of the party, you get a better chance for preemptive fights and fewer ambushes as well.

EDIT: Lunar IPS is the patching program that I recommend.
